/get_gstate
{
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE begin
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_spc currentcolorspace def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx 0 def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_comps 12 array def
	mark currentcolor counttomark
		{AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_comps AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx 3 -1 roll put
		/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx 1 add def}repeat pop
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_fnt rootfont def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_lw currentlinewidth def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_lc currentlinecap def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_lj currentlinejoin def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ml currentmiterlimit def
	currentdash/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_do xdf/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_da xdf
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_sa currentstrokeadjust def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_rnd currentcolorrendering def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_op currentoverprint def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_bg currentblackgeneration cvlit def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ucr currentundercolorremoval cvlit def
	currentcolortransfer cvlit/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_gy_xfer xdf cvlit/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_b_xfer xdf
		cvlit/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_g_xfer xdf cvlit/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_r_xfer xdf
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ht currenthalftone def
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_flt currentflat def
	end
}def
/set_gstate
{
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE begin
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_spc setcolorspace
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx{AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_comps AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx 1 sub get
	/AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_indx 1 sub def}repeat setcolor
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_fnt setfont
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_lw setlinewidth
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_lc setlinecap
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_lj setlinejoin
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ml setmiterlimit
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_da AGMUTIL_GSTATE_do setdash
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_sa setstrokeadjust
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_clr_rnd setcolorrendering
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_op setoverprint
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_bg cvx setblackgeneration
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ucr cvx setundercolorremoval
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_r_xfer cvx AGMUTIL_GSTATE_g_xfer cvx AGMUTIL_GSTATE_b_xfer cvx
		AGMUTIL_GSTATE_gy_xfer cvx setcolortransfer
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ht/HalftoneType get dup 9 eq exch 100 eq or
		{
		currenthalftone/HalftoneType get AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ht/HalftoneType get ne
			{
			 mark AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ht{sethalftone}stopped cleartomark
			}if
		}{
		AGMUTIL_GSTATE_ht sethalftone
		}ifelse
	AGMUTIL_GSTATE_flt setflat
	end
}def

/AGMUTIL_imagefile nd
/read_image_file
{
	AGMUTIL_imagefile 0 setfileposition
	10 dict begin
	/imageDict xdf
	/imbufLen Width BitsPerComponent mul 7 add 8 idiv def
	/imbufIdx 0 def
	/origDataSource imageDict/DataSource get def
	/origMultipleDataSources imageDict/MultipleDataSources get def
	/origDecode imageDict/Decode get def
	/dstDataStr imageDict/Width get colorSpaceElemCnt mul string def
	imageDict/MultipleDataSources known{MultipleDataSources}{false}ifelse
	{
		/imbufCnt imageDict/DataSource get length def
		/imbufs imbufCnt array def
		0 1 imbufCnt 1 sub{
			/imbufIdx xdf
			imbufs imbufIdx imbufLen string put
			imageDict/DataSource get imbufIdx[AGMUTIL_imagefile imbufs imbufIdx get/readstring cvx/pop cvx]cvx put
		}for
		DeviceN_PS2{
			imageDict begin
		 	/DataSource[DataSource/devn_sep_datasource cvx]cvx def
			/MultipleDataSources false def
			/Decode[0 1]def
			end
		}if
	}{
		/imbuf imbufLen string def
		Indexed_DeviceN level3 not and DeviceN_NoneName or{
			/srcDataStrs[imageDict begin
				currentdict/MultipleDataSources known{MultipleDataSources{DataSource length}{1}ifelse}{1}ifelse
				{
					Width Decode length 2 div mul cvi string
				}repeat
				end]def		
			imageDict begin
		 	/DataSource[AGMUTIL_imagefile Decode BitsPerComponent false 1/filter_indexed_devn load dstDataStr srcDataStrs devn_alt_datasource/exec cvx]cvx def
			/Decode[0 1]def
			end
		}{
			imageDict/DataSource[1 string dup 0 AGMUTIL_imagefile Decode length 2 idiv string/readstring cvx/pop cvx names_index/get cvx/put cvx]cvx put
			imageDict/Decode[0 1]put
		}ifelse
	}ifelse
	imageDict exch
	load exec
	imageDict/DataSource origDataSource put
	imageDict/MultipleDataSources origMultipleDataSources put
	imageDict/Decode origDecode put	
	end
}bdf
/write_image_file
{
	begin
	{(AGMUTIL_imagefile)(w+)file}stopped{
		false
	}{
		Adobe_AGM_Utils/AGMUTIL_imagefile xddf 
		2 dict begin
		/imbufLen Width BitsPerComponent mul 7 add 8 idiv def
		MultipleDataSources{DataSource 0 get}{DataSource}ifelse type/filetype eq{
			/imbuf imbufLen string def
		}if
		1 1 Height MultipleDataSources not{Decode length 2 idiv mul}if{
			pop
			MultipleDataSources{
			 	0 1 DataSource length 1 sub{
					DataSource type dup
					/arraytype eq{
						pop DataSource exch gx
					}{
						/filetype eq{
							DataSource exch get imbuf readstring pop
						}{
							DataSource exch get
						}ifelse
					}ifelse
					AGMUTIL_imagefile exch writestring
				}for
			}{
				DataSource type dup
				/arraytype eq{
					pop DataSource exec
				}{
					/filetype eq{
						DataSource imbuf readstring pop
					}{
						DataSource
					}ifelse
				}ifelse
				AGMUTIL_imagefile exch writestring
			}ifelse
		}for
		end
		true
	}ifelse
	end
}bdf

/consumeimagedata
{
	begin
	AGMIMG_init_common
	currentdict/MultipleDataSources known not
		{/MultipleDataSources false def}if
	MultipleDataSources
		{
		DataSource 0 get type
		dup/filetype eq
			{
			1 dict begin
			/flushbuffer Width cvi string def
			1 1 Height cvi
				{
				pop
				0 1 DataSource length 1 sub
					{
					DataSource exch get
					flushbuffer readstring pop pop
					}for
				}for
			end
			}if
		dup/arraytype eq exch/packedarraytype eq or DataSource 0 get xcheck and
			{
			Width Height mul cvi
				{
				0 1 DataSource length 1 sub
					{dup DataSource exch gx length exch 0 ne{pop}if}for
				dup 0 eq
					{pop exit}if
				sub dup 0 le
					{exit}if
				}loop
			pop
			}if		
		}
		{
		/DataSource load type 
		dup/filetype eq
			{
			1 dict begin
			/flushbuffer Width Decode length 2 idiv mul cvi string def
			1 1 Height{pop DataSource flushbuffer readstring pop pop}for
			end
			}if
		dup/arraytype eq exch/packedarraytype eq or/DataSource load xcheck and
			{
				Height Width BitsPerComponent mul 8 BitsPerComponent sub add 8 idiv Decode length 2 idiv mul mul
					{
					DataSource length dup 0 eq
						{pop exit}if
					sub dup 0 le
						{exit}if
					}loop
				pop
			}if
		}ifelse
	end

/compose_error_msg
{
	grestoreall initgraphics	
	/Helvetica findfont 10 scalefont setfont
	/AGMCORE_deltaY 100 def
	/AGMCORE_deltaX 310 def
	clippath pathbbox np pop pop 36 add exch 36 add exch moveto
	0 AGMCORE_deltaY rlineto AGMCORE_deltaX 0 rlineto
	0 AGMCORE_deltaY neg rlineto AGMCORE_deltaX neg 0 rlineto closepath
	0 AGMCORE_&setgray
	gsave 1 AGMCORE_&setgray fill grestore 
	1 setlinewidth gsave stroke grestore
	currentpoint AGMCORE_deltaY 15 sub add exch 8 add exch moveto
	/AGMCORE_deltaY 12 def
	/AGMCORE_tmp 0 def
	AGMCORE_err_strings exch get
		{
		dup 32 eq
			{
			pop
			AGMCORE_str256 0 AGMCORE_tmp getinterval
			stringwidth pop currentpoint pop add AGMCORE_deltaX 28 add gt
				{
				currentpoint AGMCORE_deltaY sub exch pop
				clippath pathbbox pop pop pop 44 add exch moveto
				}if
			AGMCORE_str256 0 AGMCORE_tmp getinterval show( )show
			0 1 AGMCORE_str256 length 1 sub
				{
				AGMCORE_str256 exch 0 put
				}for
			/AGMCORE_tmp 0 def
			}{
				AGMCORE_str256 exch AGMCORE_tmp xpt
				/AGMCORE_tmp AGMCORE_tmp 1 add def
			}ifelse
		}forall
}bdf

	/convert_spot_to_process where{pop}{

				pop false

				{
					gsave
					1 0 0 0 setcmykcolor currentgray 1 exch sub
					0 1 0 0 setcmykcolor currentgray 1 exch sub

					0 0 0 1 setcmykcolor currentgray 1 exch sub

						//Adobe_AGM_Core/AGMCORE_name xddf
						false
						//Adobe_AGM_Core/AGMCORE_pattern_paint_type get 0 eq
						AGMUTIL_cpd/OverrideSeparations known and

								{

							}if

						}{

							{

								pop pop pop true

				}ifelse
			}ifelse
			end
		}def
	}ifelse

						dup(Yellow)eq 3 -1 roll or exch

				{

					/string_out data_in length ncomp idiv string def

						}for

					}{

					/string_out 1 string def
					/component xdf
					[
					data_in string_in/readstring cvx
						[component/get cvx 255/exch cvx/sub cvx string_out/exch cvx 0/exch cvx/put cvx string_out]cvx
						[/pop cvx()]cvx/ifelse cvx
					]cvx/ReusableStreamDecode filter
				}ifelse
				end
				}def
			/AGMCORE_separateShadingFunction
				{
				2 dict begin
				/paint? xdf
				/channel xdf
				dup type/dicttype eq
					{
					begin
					FunctionType 0 eq
						{
						/DataSource channel Range length 2 idiv DataSource AGMCORE_filter_functiondatasource def
						currentdict/Decode known
							{/Decode Decode channel 2 mul 2 getinterval def}if
						paint? not
							{/Decode[1 1]def}if
						}if
					FunctionType 2 eq
						{
						paint?
							{
							/C0[C0 channel get 1 exch sub]def
							/C1[C1 channel get 1 exch sub]def
							}{
							/C0[1]def
							/C1[1]def
							}ifelse			
						}if
					FunctionType 3 eq
						{
						/Functions[Functions{channel paint? AGMCORE_separateShadingFunction}forall]def			
						}if
					currentdict/Range known
						{/Range[0 1]def}if
					currentdict
					end}{
					channel get 0 paint? AGMCORE_separateShadingFunction
					}ifelse
				end
				}def
			/AGMCORE_separateShading
				{
				3 -1 roll begin
				currentdict/Function known
					{
					currentdict/Background known
						{[1 index{Background 3 index get 1 exch sub}{1}ifelse]/Background xdf}if
					Function 3 1 roll AGMCORE_separateShadingFunction/Function xdf
					/ColorSpace[/DeviceGray]def
					}{
					ColorSpace dup type/arraytype eq{0 get}if/DeviceCMYK eq
						{
						/ColorSpace[/DeviceN[/_cyan_/_magenta_/_yellow_/_black_]/DeviceCMYK{}]def
						}{
						ColorSpace dup 1 get AGMCORE_RemoveProcessColorNames 1 exch put
						}ifelse
					ColorSpace 0 get/Separation eq
						{
							{
								[1/exch cvx/sub cvx]cvx
							}{
								[/pop cvx 1]cvx
							}ifelse
							ColorSpace 3 3 -1 roll put
							pop
						}{
							{
								[exch ColorSpace 1 get length 1 sub exch sub/index cvx 1/exch cvx/sub cvx ColorSpace 1 get length 1 add 1/roll cvx ColorSpace 1 get length{/pop cvx}repeat]cvx
							}{
								pop[ColorSpace 1 get length{/pop cvx}repeat cvx 1]cvx

		}
		ifelse
		gsave
		clippath
		x1 y1 translate
		theta rotate
		{pathbbox}stopped
		{0 0 0 0}if
		/yMax exch def
		/xMax exch def
		/yMin exch def
		/xMin exch def
		grestore
		xMax xMin eq yMax yMin eq or
		{
			grestore
			end
		}{
			rampdict begin
			20 dict begin
			background length 0 gt{background sssetbackground gsave clippath fill grestore}if
			gsave
			x1 y1 translate
			theta rotate
			/xStart 0 def
			/xEnd x2 x1 sub dup mul y2 y1 sub dup mul add 0.5 exp def
			/ySpan yMax yMin sub def
			/numsteps NumSamples def
			/rampIndxInc 1 def
			/subsampling false def
			xStart 0 transform
			xEnd 0 transform
			3 -1 roll
			sub dup mul
			3 1 roll
			sub dup mul
			add 0.5 exp 72 div
			0 72 matrix defaultmatrix dtransform dup mul exch dup mul add sqrt
			72 0 matrix defaultmatrix dtransform dup mul exch dup mul add sqrt
			1 index 1 index lt{exch}if pop
			mul
			/numpix xdf
			numpix 0 ne
			{
				NumSamples numpix div 0.5 gt
				{
					/numsteps numpix 2 div round cvi dup 1 le{pop 2}if def
					/rampIndxInc NumSamples 1 sub numsteps div def
					/subsampling true def
				}if
			}if
			ext0
			{
				0 getrampcolor
				xMin xStart lt
				{
					xMin yMin xMin neg ySpan rectfill
				}if
			}if
			/xInc xEnd xStart sub numsteps div def
			/x xStart def
			0
			numsteps
			{
				dup
				subsampling{round cvi}if
				getrampcolor
				x yMin xInc ySpan rectfill
				/x x xInc add def
				rampIndxInc add
			}repeat
			pop
			ext1{
				xMax xEnd gt
				{
					xEnd yMin xMax xEnd sub ySpan rectfill
				}if
			}if
			grestore
			grestore
			end
			end
			end
		}ifelse
	}bdf

 		}for

/setdevicencolorspace
{
	dup/AliasedColorants known{false}{true}ifelse 
	current_spot_alias and{
		7 dict begin
		/names_index 0 def
		dup/names_len exch/Names get length def
		/new_names names_len array def
		/new_LookupTables names_len array def
		/alias_cnt 0 def
		dup/Names get
		{
			dup map_alias{
				exch pop
				dup/ColorLookup known{
					dup begin
					new_LookupTables names_index ColorLookup put
					end
				}{
					dup/Components known{
						dup begin
						new_LookupTables names_index Components put
						end
					}{
						dup begin
						new_LookupTables names_index[null null null null]put
						end
					}ifelse
				}ifelse
				new_names names_index 3 -1 roll/Name get put
				/alias_cnt alias_cnt 1 add def 
			}{
				/name xdf				
				new_names names_index name put
				dup/LookupTables known{
					dup begin
					new_LookupTables names_index LookupTables names_index get put
					end
				}{
					dup begin
					new_LookupTables names_index[null null null null]put
					end
				}ifelse
			}ifelse
			/names_index names_index 1 add def 
		}forall
		alias_cnt 0 gt{
			/AliasedColorants true def
			/lut_entry_len new_LookupTables 0 get dup length 256 ge{0 get length}{length}ifelse def
			0 1 names_len 1 sub{
				/names_index xdf
				new_LookupTables names_index get dup length 256 ge{0 get length}{length}ifelse lut_entry_len ne{
					/AliasedColorants false def
					exit
				}{
					new_LookupTables names_index get 0 get null eq{
						dup/Names get names_index get/name xdf
						name(Cyan)eq name(Magenta)eq name(Yellow)eq name(Black)eq
						or or or not{
							/AliasedColorants false def
							exit
						}if
					}if
				}ifelse
			}for
			lut_entry_len 1 eq{
				/AliasedColorants false def
			}if
			AliasedColorants{
				dup begin
				/Names new_names def
				/LookupTables new_LookupTables def
				/AliasedColorants true def
				/NComponents lut_entry_len def
				/TintMethod NComponents 4 eq{/Subtractive}{/Additive}ifelse def
				/MappedCSA TintMethod/Additive eq{/DeviceRGB}{/DeviceCMYK}ifelse def
				currentdict/TTTablesIdx known not{
					/TTTablesIdx -1 def
				}if
				end
			}if
		}if
		end
	}if
	dup/devicen_colorspace_dict exch AGMCORE_gput
	begin
	currentdict/AliasedColorants known{
		AliasedColorants
	}{
		false
	}ifelse
	dup not{
		CSA map_csa
	}if
	/TintTransform load type/nulltype eq or{
		/TintTransform[
			0 1 Names length 1 sub
				{
				/TTTablesIdx TTTablesIdx 1 add def
				dup LookupTables exch get dup 0 get null eq
					{
					1 index
					Names exch get
					dup(Cyan)eq
						{
						pop exch
						LookupTables length exch sub
						/index cvx
						0 0 0
						}
						{
						dup(Magenta)eq
							{
							pop exch
							LookupTables length exch sub
							/index cvx
							0/exch cvx 0 0
							}{
							(Yellow)eq
								{
								exch
								LookupTables length exch sub
								/index cvx
								0 0 3 -1/roll cvx 0
								}{
								exch
								LookupTables length exch sub
								/index cvx
								0 0 0 4 -1/roll cvx
								}ifelse
							}ifelse
						}ifelse
					5 -1/roll cvx/astore cvx
					}{
					dup length 1 sub
					LookupTables length 4 -1 roll sub 1 add
					/index cvx/mul cvx/round cvx/cvi cvx/get cvx
					}ifelse
					Names length TTTablesIdx add 1 add 1/roll cvx
				}for
			Names length[/pop cvx]cvx/repeat cvx
			NComponents Names length
 			TintMethod/Subtractive eq
 				{
 				subtractive_blend
 				}{
 				additive_blend
 				}ifelse
		]cvx bdf
	}if
	AGMCORE_host_sep{
		Names convert_to_process{
			exec_tint_transform
		}
		{	
			currentdict/AliasedColorants known{
				AliasedColorants not
			}{
				false
			}ifelse
			5 dict begin
			/AvoidAliasedColorants xdf
			/painted? false def
			/names_index 0 def
			/names_len Names length def
			AvoidAliasedColorants{
				/currentspotalias current_spot_alias def
				false set_spot_alias
			}if
			Names{
				AGMCORE_is_cmyk_sep{
					dup(Cyan)eq AGMCORE_cyan_plate and exch
					dup(Magenta)eq AGMCORE_magenta_plate and exch
					dup(Yellow)eq AGMCORE_yellow_plate and exch
					(Black)eq AGMCORE_black_plate and or or or{
						/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/TintProc[
							Names names_index/devn_makecustomcolor cvx
						]cvx ddf
						/painted? true def
					}if
					painted?{exit}if
				}{
					0 0 0 0 5 -1 roll findcmykcustomcolor 1 setcustomcolor currentgray 0 eq{
					/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/TintProc[
						Names names_index/devn_makecustomcolor cvx
					]cvx ddf
					/painted? true def
					exit
					}if
				}ifelse
				/names_index names_index 1 add def
			}forall
			AvoidAliasedColorants{
				currentspotalias set_spot_alias
			}if
			painted?{
				/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/names_index names_index put
			}{
				/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/TintProc[
					names_len[/pop cvx]cvx/repeat cvx 1/setseparationgray cvx
 					0 0 0 0/setcmykcolor cvx
				]cvx ddf
			}ifelse
			end
		}ifelse
	}
	{
		AGMCORE_in_rip_sep{
			Names convert_to_process not
		}{
			level3
		}ifelse
		{
			[/DeviceN Names MappedCSA/TintTransform load]setcolorspace_opt
			/TintProc level3 not AGMCORE_in_rip_sep and{
				[
					Names/length cvx[/pop cvx]cvx/repeat cvx
				]cvx bdf
			}{
				{setcolor}bdf
			}ifelse
		}{
			exec_tint_transform
		}ifelse
	}ifelse
	set_crd
	/AliasedColorants false def
	end
}def

/make_pattern
{
	exch clonedict exch
	dup matrix currentmatrix matrix concatmatrix 0 0 3 2 roll itransform
	exch 3 index/XStep get 1 index exch 2 copy div cvi mul sub sub
	exch 3 index/YStep get 1 index exch 2 copy div cvi mul sub sub
	matrix translate exch matrix concatmatrix
			 1 index begin
		BBox 0 get XStep div cvi XStep mul/xshift exch neg def
		BBox 1 get YStep div cvi YStep mul/yshift exch neg def
		BBox 0 get xshift add
		BBox 1 get yshift add
		BBox 2 get xshift add
		BBox 3 get yshift add
		4 array astore
		/BBox exch def
		[xshift yshift/translate load null/exec load]dup
		3/PaintProc load put cvx/PaintProc exch def
		end
	gsave 0 setgray
	makepattern
	grestore

						/p1x r2 SS1 SS1 mul SS1 SS1 mul 1 add div sqrt mul neg def
						/p1y c2y p1x SS1 div sub def
						/SS2 90 theta sub dup sin exch cos div def
						/p2x r2 SS2 SS2 mul SS2 SS2 mul 1 add div sqrt mul def
						/p2y c2y p2x SS2 div sub def

							/L2maxX p2x yMax p2y sub SS2 div add def

						}ifelse
						p1x p1y moveto p2x p2y lineto L2maxX L2maxX p2x sub SS2 mul p2y add lineto
						L1maxX L1maxX p1x sub SS1 mul p1y add lineto
						fill

		end
		end
		}ifelse

	/GenStrips

			0 BBox 3 get BBox 1 get sub rlineto
			BBox 2 get BBox 0 get sub neg 0 rlineto

		/xMin exch def
		grestore

		{

			end
		}{
			rampdict begin
			20 dict begin
			background length 0 gt{background sssetbackground gsave clippath fill grestore}if
			gsave
			x1 y1 translate
			theta rotate
			/xStart 0 def
			/xEnd x2 x1 sub dup mul y2 y1 sub dup mul add 0.5 exp def
			/ySpan yMax yMin sub def
			/numsteps NumSamples def
			/rampIndxInc 1 def
			/subsampling false def

			xEnd 0 transform
			3 -1 roll

			sub dup mul

			72 0 matrix defaultmatrix dtransform dup mul exch dup mul add sqrt
			1 index 1 index lt{exch}if pop

			}if

			}if
			/xInc xEnd xStart sub numsteps div def
			/x xStart def
			0

			{
				dup
				subsampling{round cvi}if
				getrampcolor

				/x x xInc add def
				rampIndxInc add

/additive_blend

 			{

 		numarrays 1 add 1/roll cvx 
 		}for
 	numarrays[/pop cvx]cvx/repeat cvx
 	end
}def
/subtractive_blend

			c1/get cvx/sub cvx/mul cvx
			}for
		/sub cvx

		}for
	numarrays[/pop cvx]cvx/repeat cvx
	end

/setdevicencolorspace
{
	dup/AliasedColorants known{false}{true}ifelse

		7 dict begin
		/names_index 0 def
		dup/names_len exch/Names get length def
		/new_names names_len array def
		/new_LookupTables names_len array def
		/alias_cnt 0 def
		dup/Names get
		{
			dup map_alias{
				exch pop
				dup/ColorLookup known{
					dup begin
					new_LookupTables names_index ColorLookup put
					end
				}{

				}ifelse
				new_names names_index 3 -1 roll/Name get put
				/alias_cnt alias_cnt 1 add def 
			}{
				/name xdf				
				new_names names_index name put
				dup/LookupTables known{
					dup begin
					new_LookupTables names_index LookupTables names_index get put
					end
				}{
					dup begin
					new_LookupTables names_index[null null null null]put
					end
				}ifelse
			}ifelse
			/names_index names_index 1 add def 
		}forall
		alias_cnt 0 gt{
			/AliasedColorants true def
			/lut_entry_len new_LookupTables 0 get dup length 256 ge{0 get length}{length}ifelse def
			0 1 names_len 1 sub{
				/names_index xdf
				new_LookupTables names_index get dup length 256 ge{0 get length}{length}ifelse lut_entry_len ne{
					/AliasedColorants false def
					exit
				}{
					new_LookupTables names_index get 0 get null eq{
						dup/Names get names_index get/name xdf
						name(Cyan)eq name(Magenta)eq name(Yellow)eq name(Black)eq
						or or or not{
							/AliasedColorants false def
							exit
						}if
					}if
				}ifelse
			}for
			lut_entry_len 1 eq{
				/AliasedColorants false def
			}if
			AliasedColorants{
				dup begin
				/Names new_names def
				/LookupTables new_LookupTables def
				/AliasedColorants true def
				/NComponents lut_entry_len def
				/TintMethod NComponents 4 eq{/Subtractive}{/Additive}ifelse def
				/MappedCSA TintMethod/Additive eq{/DeviceRGB}{/DeviceCMYK}ifelse def
				currentdict/TTTablesIdx known not{
					/TTTablesIdx -1 def
				}if
				end

		}if
		end

	dup/devicen_colorspace_dict exch AGMCORE_gput
	begin
	currentdict/AliasedColorants known{
		AliasedColorants
	}{
		false
	}ifelse
	dup not{
		CSA map_csa
	}if
	/TintTransform load type/nulltype eq or{
		/TintTransform[
			0 1 Names length 1 sub
				{
				/TTTablesIdx TTTablesIdx 1 add def
				dup LookupTables exch get dup 0 get null eq
					{
					1 index
					Names exch get
					dup(Cyan)eq
						{
						pop exch
						LookupTables length exch sub
						/index cvx
						0 0 0
						}
						{
						dup(Magenta)eq
							{
							pop exch
							LookupTables length exch sub
							/index cvx
							0/exch cvx 0 0
							}{
							(Yellow)eq
								{
								exch
								LookupTables length exch sub
								/index cvx
								0 0 3 -1/roll cvx 0
								}{
								exch
								LookupTables length exch sub
								/index cvx
								0 0 0 4 -1/roll cvx
								}ifelse
							}ifelse
						}ifelse
					5 -1/roll cvx/astore cvx
					}{
					dup length 1 sub
					LookupTables length 4 -1 roll sub 1 add
					/index cvx/mul cvx/round cvx/cvi cvx/get cvx
					}ifelse
					Names length TTTablesIdx add 1 add 1/roll cvx
				}for
			Names length[/pop cvx]cvx/repeat cvx
			NComponents Names length
 			TintMethod/Subtractive eq
 				{
 				subtractive_blend
 				}{
 				additive_blend

		]cvx bdf

	AGMCORE_host_sep{

		{

			5 dict begin

			/painted? false def
			/names_index 0 def
			/names_len Names length def
			AvoidAliasedColorants{
				/currentspotalias current_spot_alias def
				false set_spot_alias
			}if
			Names{
				AGMCORE_is_cmyk_sep{
					dup(Cyan)eq AGMCORE_cyan_plate and exch
					dup(Magenta)eq AGMCORE_magenta_plate and exch
					dup(Yellow)eq AGMCORE_yellow_plate and exch
					(Black)eq AGMCORE_black_plate and or or or{
						/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/TintProc[
							Names names_index/devn_makecustomcolor cvx
						]cvx ddf
						/painted? true def
					}if
					painted?{exit}if
				}{
					0 0 0 0 5 -1 roll findcmykcustomcolor 1 setcustomcolor currentgray 0 eq{
					/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/TintProc[
						Names names_index/devn_makecustomcolor cvx
					]cvx ddf
					/painted? true def
					exit
					}if
				}ifelse
				/names_index names_index 1 add def
			}forall
			AvoidAliasedColorants{
				currentspotalias set_spot_alias
			}if
			painted?{
				/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/names_index names_index put
			}{
				/devicen_colorspace_dict AGMCORE_gget/TintProc[
					names_len[/pop cvx]cvx/repeat cvx 1/setseparationgray cvx
 					0 0 0 0/setcmykcolor cvx
				]cvx ddf
			}ifelse
			end
		}ifelse
	}
	{
		AGMCORE_in_rip_sep{
			Names convert_to_process not
		}{
			level3
		}ifelse
		{
			[/DeviceN Names MappedCSA/TintTransform load]setcolorspace_opt
			/TintProc level3 not AGMCORE_in_rip_sep and{

			}ifelse
		}{
			exec_tint_transform
		}ifelse
	}ifelse
	set_crd
	/AliasedColorants false def
	end

﻿\section{Purpose, source version, and reading instructions}

This revised second report documents the core Python implementation as of 28 October 2026 of the aircraft-maintenance tutorial, including the environment and all implemented learning methods. It supersedes the implementation descriptions in the report dated 22 October 2026. That earlier report correctly described a single fleet controller at its own source version; its statement that multi-agent learning was not implemented no longer describes the current code.

We retain the method comparisons and the complete source walkthrough from the second report dated 26 October 2026. The revision follows the subsequent code cleanup. The simulator remains a research tutorial with synthetic assumptions, and the software checks do not establish operational validity.

\textbf{Code scope.} As in the previous report, the detailed walkthrough covers \texttt{maintenance\_\allowbreak{}tutorial\_\allowbreak{}annotated\_\allowbreak{}core.\allowbreak{}py}. The notebook assembles this file with the separate exercises/solutions and behavioral-test files into one in-memory module. \section{What changed since the earlier code report}

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
\item Aircraft have stable fleet-local plate labels, such as \texttt{AC-001}, linking their array indices, actions, maintenance jobs, and event diagnostics. These labels do not by themselves create a persistent flight-history database or a fleet-status bitmask.
\item Crew members and workshops have identities and individual duration factors. Crew selection is an identity bitmask. Selected crew work rates add; a workshop factor changes component work duration. A job stores cumulative component-completion days so accepted scheduling assumptions are used during actual execution.
\item Observation version 3 retains 70 values per aircraft and extends public information with individual resource availability and factor encodings. Fleet and resource counts are configurable at model construction.
\item Multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) supports aircraft ownership with shared actor weights and component-type ownership with six independent actors. Its centralized training critic produces one value per agent; actors use restricted observed information.
\item Deep centralized multi-agent actor--critic (DCMAC) and deep decentralized multi-agent actor--critic (DDMAC) have separate off-policy fleet adaptations under aircraft and component-type ownership. They receive global observed beliefs, use replay and joint importance-weighted temporal-difference (TD) updates, and have one scalar fleet critic.
\item A daily aircraft-option wrapper permits new plans for free aircraft while other aircraft remain in committed repairs. Additional methods implement separate learned planning stages, replacement-budget targets, a single-aircraft MAXQ-0 baseline, safe planning-mode option-critic, and a two-level value-decomposition adaptation. A restricted-catalog flat comparator accompanies them.
\item The common model factory, training dispatcher, evaluation, checkpoints, runner, tests, and comprehensive notebook recognize the additions. The notebook has ten learning parts and 122 executed code cells; the behavioral suite records 45 passing tests after the cleanup.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Not implemented by these changes.} Explicit flight legs, flight-hour duration, time/cycle-dependent wear, thermal/dust/salt condition inputs, standardized common-reference post-landing measurements, and the richer bird/hail encounter model remain pending. The current weather multiplier and incident constants must not be described as the completed literature-based upgrade.

\section{Cleanup applied on 28 October 2026}

\subsection{Source size and retained methods}

The core decreased from 4,273 to 2,331 physical lines, a reduction of 1,942 lines (45.4\%). We removed 1,936 generated \texttt{\# Explanation:} comments and nine duplicate imports. The reduction therefore comes mainly from inline documentation. No existing function or method was removed. All 18 learned methods, network constructors, registered layers, reward formulas, physical transitions, observation/action layouts, training losses and trainer functions were retained.

Eight existing function or method bodies changed, and one private helper was added. The changes below concern repeated input handling and unnecessary intermediate work. Registered layers that are unused in particular modes remain present so existing checkpoint keys and parameter initialization order remain compatible.

\subsection{Shared observation validation}

\texttt{\_fleet\_observation\_tensor} converts observations to float32 tensors, adds a batch dimension to a single observation, and checks the expected two-dimensional width. MAPPO input preparation, DCMAC input preparation and the two hierarchy feature adapters reuse this helper. Their shape requirements and error messages remain the same. The helper validates the global observation without constructing local actor features.

\subsection{Direct critic evaluation}

\texttt{AircraftPlanningHierarchy.value} and \texttt{FleetOptionCritic.q\_values} now pass the validated observation directly to their existing critic networks. Previously, these calls constructed actor context through \texttt{features()} and discarded that context. The option-value path retains its original output reshape. Neither change removes a critic or changes its layers.

An isolated forward-call benchmark recorded speedups of 1.87 to 2.03 times at seven aircraft and 7.88 to 8.17 times at 50 aircraft. It used batches of 32, one Torch CPU thread, disabled gradients, alternating old/new measurement order and five timing blocks. These measurements concern the two critic calls only. The calculated avoided actor-context allocation was 519,680 bytes at seven aircraft and 22,976,000 bytes at 50 aircraft. These values are not measured peak-memory reductions, and no GPU, backward-pass or full-training speedup was established.

The direct calls also change an extension point: an external subclass or monkeypatch that intercepts \texttt{features()} will no longer intercept these critic methods. The built-in implementations do not rely on that interception.

\subsection{Action history and input validity}

\texttt{FleetActorCritic.act} skips the previous-choice buffer in flat mode because that mode does not use it to condition logits. Other modes still update the history needed by later fields, but skip the final update after the last field. Feasibility masks, action probabilities, action reconstruction and sampling are retained. The history update remains out of place because earlier conditioning layers may retain their inputs for backpropagation.

\texttt{FleetMaintenanceEnv.reset} now explicitly requires finite custom initial health, in addition to the existing shape and range checks. NaN values previously passed the range comparisons and now raise \texttt{ValueError}. Positive and negative infinity already failed the previous range check. Valid finite arrays in $[0,1]$ retain their previous initialization behavior.

\subsection{Verification scope and documentation}

The recorded checks support preserved built-in behavior for the valid inputs they exercise. They do not prove equivalence for every configuration. The saved verification JSON does not include source hashes or environment versions, so it is a record of the earlier verification rather than a fully self-contained reproducibility package. This report embeds the current code and records its source hash for navigation and version identification.

The teaching explanations remain in the reports. Current listings and explanation labels below use the cleaned source line numbers. Older reports and historical timing manifests retain their original version context. The abstract was not regenerated; this technical report has no abstract section.

\section{The environment, policy, trainer, and evaluator}

\subsection{Four responsibilities}

The \textbf{environment} owns hidden health, synthetic measurements, estimated condition, inventory, crews, workshops, committed jobs, rewards, and the physical clock. A policy submits a decision; the simulator decides whether and how it can be executed. The policy does not directly write true health or change a running repair.

The \textbf{policy} maps permitted information to decisions. An actor produces action probabilities. A value learner estimates future return, either as a state value or an action/option value. Reinforcement learning (RL) updates these estimates from interaction; hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) introduces specified planning levels or temporally extended behavior. A physically nested component structure does not alone define an HRL algorithm \cite{suttonbook,sutton1999}.

The \textbf{trainer} collects transitions, constructs targets, computes losses, and updates network parameters or tables. Different trainers in this file use different algorithms: proximal policy optimization (PPO), MAPPO, replay-based actor--critic, MAXQ completion-value learning, option-critic gradients, or hierarchical value-decomposition targets. They share a simulator, not one universal loss \cite{ppo2017}.

The \textbf{evaluator} creates fresh seeded episodes and requests fixed-weight decisions. It does not call an optimizer. It reconstructs the required option state at episode start. For neural categorical policies it normally chooses the most likely action; option-critic also uses a deterministic threshold for termination. These deterministic evaluation conventions differ from the stochastic choices used during training.

\subsection{The notebook's library trainer versus the custom fleet trainers}

Stable-Baselines3 (SB3) PPO is used in the introductory notebook example with \texttt{GymMaintenanceEnv}. The custom fleet models are independently constructed by \texttt{make\_model} and updated by the appropriate custom training function. SB3 does not initialize these fleet weights and then pass them to a second optimizer.

The custom implementations make conditional action likelihoods, masks, per-agent statistics, option durations, and completion values explicit. Standard SB3 policies do not automatically implement those project-specific interfaces. This is an implementation and teaching choice, not a claim that SB3 cannot be extended. \texttt{FlattenFleetAction} only reshapes an action; it supplies neither conditional sampling nor a hierarchical training algorithm \cite{sb3docs}.

\subsection{One day is the physical time unit}

\texttt{FleetMaintenanceEnv.step} advances one day. Each eligible aircraft performs one modeled operating flight that day; a grounded aircraft does not. This is not an explicit route or multi-leg schedule. Maintenance occupies several days. Other aircraft continue operating while a job progresses.

Grounding, engine choice, bundle choice, crew selection, and workshop selection may be calculated through several Python calls before that one day advances. Those calls are computational planning stages. The older \texttt{execute\_option} instead advances the entire fleet through several days before returning to its manager. The new \texttt{AircraftOptionEnv} always returns after one day and tracks each aircraft's committed physical option independently. These two interfaces therefore provide different manager decision opportunities.

\section{State, observations, identities, and maintenance actions}

\subsection{Hidden plant and observed belief}

For \(N\) aircraft, hidden health has shape \((N,2,6)\). The six component types are fan, low-pressure compressor (LPC), high-pressure compressor (HPC), combustor, high-pressure turbine (HPT), and low-pressure turbine (LPT). Health is a normalized teaching variable, not a calibrated component map. A noisy synthetic efficiency/temperature model feeds a bootstrap particle filter. The controller observes estimates and uncertainty summaries, not the realized incident severity or hidden health array.

Each aircraft contributes 70 local values. The public vector has
\[
 P=10+2C+2W,\qquad D=70N+P,
\]
where \(C\) is crew count, \(W\) workshop count, and \(D\) total observed width. With seven aircraft, three crew members and two workshops, \(P=20\) and \(D=510\). The earlier report's 500-value example belonged to the older ten-public-value layout.

\begin{longtable}{@{}P{0.20\textwidth}P{0.24\textwidth}P{0.48\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
Local indices & Contents & Interpretation\\\midrule\endhead
0--11 & Estimated health means & Two engines times six components.\\
12--23 & Estimated standard deviations & Component uncertainty, not wear rates.\\
24--35 & Lower health quantiles & Used for conservative urgency and grounding.\\
36 & Exposure divided by 1.5 & Fixed synthetic episode context; not flight hours.\\
37--38 & Busy flag and remaining-job fraction & Whether a committed repair occupies the aircraft.\\
39--44 & Committed plan fields & Engines, two bundles, crew identity mask, workshop and cyclic order start, all normalized.\\
45--56 & Efficiency proxies & Synthetic readings, not directly observed physical health modifiers.\\
57--68 & Normalized temperature proxies & Encoded through the fixed Celsius range.\\
69 & Reading age divided by horizon & Increases while grounded because no new flight measurement is collected.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

Public indices 0--9 contain day, free-resource fractions, replenishment timing and six stock values. Next come crew free flags, crew factor encodings, workshop free flags and workshop factor encodings. A duration factor \(f\) is encoded as \(1/(1+f)\); its meaning remains a maintenance-time factor, not a direct reward bonus.

\subsection{Bitwise selection and aircraft plates}

For a component index \(c\), \texttt{1 << c} sets one bit. Decimal 5 is \(000101_2\), selecting fan and HPC on one engine. The two engine bits identify which engine bundles are nonempty; they do not replace the component bundles. Similarly, \texttt{0b101} selects crew members 0 and 2. Bitwise AND tests membership, bitwise OR combines selections, and \texttt{bit\_count()} counts selected members.

The workshop is a single integer index, not a bitmask. Aircraft plates are stable strings mapped to array indices, not a one-hot observation or a binary fleet status. Identity, availability, and operating history are separate concepts. Reset retains the plate/index mapping but starts a new episode history.

\subsection{Full eight-field action and duration}

The original daily fleet policies choose
\begin{minted}[linenos=false]{python}
[ground, engine_mask, bundle0, bundle1,
 crew_mask, workshop_index, order_start, priority]
\end{minted}
for every aircraft. Their category counts are
\[
 [2,4,64,64,2^C,W,12,N].
\]
The 64 bundle categories are the \(2^6\) possible subsets. The crew head grows as \(2^C\), an explicit combinatorial limitation. A nonempty new repair requires a nonzero crew identity mask. Priority determines proposal processing order. \texttt{order\_start} selects a cyclic order of engine/component slots, not an arbitrary permutation of selected tasks.

For crew set \(S\), component labor \(L_c\), and workshop factor \(f_w\),
\[
 R_S=\sum_{i\in S}\frac{1}{f_i},\qquad
 d_c=\max\!\left(1,\left\lceil\frac{L_c f_w}{R_S}\right\rceil\right),\qquad
 d_{job}=d_{setup}+\sum_c d_c.
\]
Setup is fixed; component tasks execute sequentially. The stored cumulative completion days determine when each component is restored. Faster crew or workshop factors can reduce work time; they do not remove setup or create a new negative cost term. These are synthetic additive-work-rate assumptions.

\subsection{Reservations, costs, and observation updates}

Accepted plans reserve identified crew members and a workshop and consume selected spares. A busy aircraft's new row cannot replace the plan. Components restore to health one at their completion thresholds. The aircraft remains grounded until the entire job completes, and readings remain old until another flight.

The current cost includes setup, selected engines, parts, unused-life cost, downtime, failures, and rejected requests. Daily reward is \((10\,flights-cost)/(10N)\). The unsafe-flight hold uses the minimum observed lower health quantile over all components; it does not require HPC to fail first. Job duration is derived from the package and resources, rather than freely selected as a duration action. Spares are selected indirectly through replacement content; procurement and ordering are not learned actions.

\section{Single-agent policies, shared parameters, and multi-agent information}

\subsection{Four independent design questions}

Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) requires specifying decision ownership and learning, not merely counting network objects. The following choices should be stated separately:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
\item \textbf{Ownership:} one joint fleet controller, one agent per aircraft, or one agent per component type across aircraft.
\item \textbf{Information:} global observed fleet belief, aircraft-local information plus public variables, or a component-restricted view.
\item \textbf{Parameters:} shared actor weights, a central actor with distinct output blocks, or separately parameterized actors.
\item \textbf{Learning:} a fleet-joint PPO objective, per-agent MAPPO clipping, replay-based actor--critic, or a hierarchical/value-decomposition update.
\end{enumerate}

Centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) is an information pattern, not a competing algorithm alongside PPO or DCMAC. In the present MAPPO methods the critic uses the full observed fleet input during training and the actors can execute from their restricted inputs. However, a fixed centralized broker still allocates resources. Actor proposal generation is decentralized; complete maintenance allocation is not fully decentralized.

\subsection{Why one shared actor is not the original joint fleet controller}

The original \texttt{conditional} policy includes a learned whole-fleet encoding when constructing each aircraft row and combines action likelihoods into one fleet likelihood. Aircraft MAPPO applies one shared actor to separate local/public observations and retains a log probability and advantage per agent. Thus the same network count can conceal different information and update rules.

The original \texttt{shared} mode is an important qualification: it also reuses local/public actor weights. It remains in the original fleet-joint update and full-action interface. It is closer in information structure to aircraft MAPPO, but it is not the new MAPPO objective or request-only action interface. In fact, \texttt{flat}, \texttt{conditional}, and \texttt{shared} all reuse their actor and field heads across aircraft. The name \texttt{shared} chiefly distinguishes omission of learned global actor context.

\subsection{Why single-agent flat PPO is not DCMAC despite similar network counts}

The \texttt{flat} baseline already has factorized categorical fields; it is not a network enumerating every possible joint action. DCMAC also uses factorized outputs, but the implemented DCMAC family defines aircraft/component control units, uses the replacement-request interface and fixed broker, and trains a global actor and scalar critic from replay with a joint truncated importance ratio. The original fleet PPO instead learns eight fields and optimizes clipped on-policy-style fleet likelihoods. A one-actor/one-critic count does not equate these implementations \cite{dcmac2019}.

\subsection{Why DDMAC has N networks and still needs global observations}

Aircraft DDMAC sets its actor count from \texttt{len(env.aircraft\_plates)}. Each list-comprehension iteration constructs a new network, so seven aircraft create seven independent parameter sets. All actors nevertheless receive the same global observed fleet vector; each owns only its own replacement request. This follows the global-belief actor convention discussed in the cited DDMAC formulation, rather than local-information execution \cite{ddmac2021}.

DCMAC's single global actor has different output blocks for different units. Its shared trunk is not the same as repeatedly applying an identical local actor. Component-type DDMAC keeps six actors as fleet size changes, but each actor's inputs and output count still grow with \(N\). Changing \(N\) constructs a new model and normally requires retraining; it does not dynamically add networks to an already running checkpoint.

\subsection{Critic sharing is a separate choice}

The original fleet PPO and DCMAC/DDMAC have one scalar state-value critic. MAPPO and the new planning-PPO modes use one centralized network with a separate output per agent/aircraft. This is one network with multiple value heads, not N separate critic networks. Option-critic has option-action values, MAXQ stores primitive/completion values, and hierarchical value-decomposition networks (VDN) sum learned agent Q values. They should not all be called the same critic architecture.

Separate local critics, a separate global critic per agent, independent local-input aircraft MAPPO actors, and shared component MAPPO actors are not additional configuration choices in the current registry. Their conceptual feasibility should not be reported as implementation.

\section{Training equations and what their axes mean}

\subsection{Fleet-joint PPO and per-agent MAPPO}

The original full-action fleet methods sum log probabilities across fields and aircraft. PPO compares the same stored fleet action under current and collection-time policies. MAPPO sums only fields belonging to one agent, preserving the agent axis before clipping. Their ratios are respectively
\[
 r_t^{fleet}=\exp\left(\sum_i\log\pi_i^{new}-\sum_i\log\pi_i^{old}\right),\qquad
 r_{t,i}=\exp\left(\log\pi_i^{new}-\log\pi_i^{old}\right).
\]
Clipping the product is not the same operation as clipping each ratio. For positive unit advantages and individual ratios 2 and 0.5, the averaged per-agent clipped surrogate is \((1.2+0.5)/2=0.85\), while the joint ratio is one. This explains a concrete code difference without attributing fleet performance to a benchmark paper \cite{mappo2022}.

\subsection{Replay-based DCMAC and DDMAC}

The code stores original submitted proposal likelihoods even when the broker defers the request. For replay behavior policy \(\mu\) and current policy \(\pi\), it calculates
\[
 w=\min\left(2,\exp\left[\sum_i\log\pi_i(a_i\mid b)-\sum_i\log\mu_i(a_i\mid b)\right]\right),
\]
\[
y=r+\gamma(1-d)V(b'),\qquad\delta=y-V(b).
\]
The actor minimizes \(-\mathbb E[w\log\pi(a\mid b)\,\mathrm{stopgrad}(\delta)]\), and the critic minimizes \(\tfrac12\mathbb E[w\delta^2]\). Weights and next-state targets are detached. The cap 2 and small-network settings are tutorial choices. Replay truncation trades variance for bias; no replay state-distribution correction is implemented. These weights correct policy likelihood mismatch, not oversampling of rare hazard scenarios.

\subsection{Aircraft option durations and completion values}

For rewards accumulated over \(k\) physical days, the new aircraft-option target is
\[
 y=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\gamma^j r_j+\gamma^k(1-d)V(b_{next}).
\]
A training-budget cutoff can bootstrap from a still-busy state; it does not cancel the job or claim option completion. Pending decisions retain their collection-time likelihoods across rollout updates. This is a delayed-decision PPO adaptation, not an assertion that all later samples are freshly on-policy. The critic also learns daily targets, including busy states.

MAXQ-0 uses a different decomposition, \(Q(i,s,a)=V(a,s)+C(i,s,a)\), where primitive V values estimate immediate reward and C estimates future reward needed to complete the parent after the child. The code updates C with the parent's continuation value discounted over the actual child duration. Quantizing observed beliefs can alias states, so exact-state guarantees are not claimed \cite{dietterich2000}.

\subsection{Option-critic termination and two-level value-decomposition networks}

Option-critic constructs a continuation value
\[
 U(b',o)=(1-\beta_{safe})Q_\Omega(b',o)+\beta_{safe}\max_{o'}Q_\Omega(b',o').
\]
Here \(\beta_{safe}=0\) while physical repair is committed. The internal policy receives a detached TD advantage. The termination network uses an option-advantage loss with a 0.01 margin at permitted nonterminal free-aircraft states only. This learns planning-mode termination without acquiring permission to interrupt repair \cite{bacon2017}.

The hierarchical value-decomposition network (VDN) adaptation sums agent values at the high and low levels. The high target uses a three-day-or-shorter macro return. The low reward adds \(0.1\delta_H/k\), using the detached high-level TD advantage \(\delta_H\) over macro duration \(k\). This coupling changes the low-level objective. The implementation draws on hierarchical cooperative coordination, but does not reproduce the complete hierarchical cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with dual coordination mechanism (HAVEN) or the nonlinear value mixer used by QMIX \cite{haven2023,vdn2018}.

\section{Comparison design, verification, and remaining work}

\subsection{Which comparisons isolate which changes}

The closest new representation comparison is \texttt{hrl\_flat} versus \texttt{planning\_hierarchy}: both have global/local inputs, the same 22 catalog requests, the same fixed resource broker, the same aircraft-specific decision opportunities, critic shape, duration accounting and PPO update. Their network parameterization and parameter counts differ. Aggregate targets retain the same union of possible requests but change the upper action semantics. The concurrent-options worker is fixed and therefore restricts realized choices further.

The six MAPPO/DCMAC/DDMAC variants share their broader replacement-request interface and broker, but differ in actor information, sharing, critic outputs, or update. They cannot be treated as a single-factor agent-count ablation. The original full-action PPO methods also learn resource fields, whereas all request methods and the new catalog methods delegate those fields. Older fleet options reduce manager opportunities. VDN changes macro timing and shaped reward. MAXQ supports one aircraft only. Equal simulation days do not equalize gradient updates, network size, or wall-clock effort.

\subsection{Recorded software checks}

The cleanup verification records 45 passing behavioral tests, including the earlier checks of environment contracts, identities, resource reservations, committed work, observation boundaries, likelihoods, targets, gradients and checkpoint round trips. Two additional tests cover direct critic evaluation without actor-context construction and rejection of nonfinite initial health. These are software assertions, not 45 independent before-and-after equivalence experiments.

For each of the 18 learned methods, the old and cleaned source were also trained for 64 simulated days with training seed 771, horizon 12, 16 particles and rollout size 16 where applicable. MAXQ used one aircraft and the other methods used two. Training logs and final state dictionaries matched exactly, and evaluation records matched at seed 10421. One historical seed-0 checkpoint per method also loaded with identical configuration and state and produced matching evaluation records at seed 10000. Those checkpoint comparisons used seven aircraft except for single-aircraft MAXQ. They do not cover every saved checkpoint or exact optimizer/replay resumption.

The two optimized critic paths produced exactly matching outputs and input gradients on one three-aircraft observation. This check does not establish equality for every input, device or batch shape. The earlier execution of all 122 code cells in the comprehensive notebook remains a historical result. The cleanup changed 52 Markdown cells, while its code cells, outputs and execution counts were retained. Neither that notebook nor the full presentation experiment was rerun for this report revision.

The presentation experiment used 1,024 training days per seed, three training seeds and 20 evaluation seeds. Its saved timings describe the earlier source snapshot. The short cleanup comparisons establish compatibility within the tested cases; they do not establish convergence, a performance ranking or improved end-to-end training time.

\subsection{Important physical and methodological limits}

The particle filter returns condition summaries, not a remaining-useful-life forecast. It resamples component marginals independently, so common physical weather does not create a fully dependency-aware Bayesian filter. Temperature still includes the aircraft-specific exposure offset. Bird/hail events are sampled independently per engine, with uniform severities and fixed component weight vectors; there is no aircraft encounter stage, explicit no-damage branch, or separate operability state.

The 22-entry menu is structurally defined, not a guarantee of stock feasibility. For example, one aircraft initially has one spare per component type, so a request for the same component on both engines needs more stock than is present under that configuration. The broker can defer it. Repair order changes component restoration timing, but the current whole-job grounding rule can leave total return unchanged for a fixed package. An earlier read-only two-task probe observed exactly that behavior.

Calendar-based staffing, graph/attention/hypergraph policies, learned peer messaging, arbitrary task permutations, procurement decisions, rolling-horizon or mixed-integer baselines, a fleet exact-search oracle, calibrated hazard parameters, rare-event confidence intervals, and unchanged-weight transfer across fleet sizes remain outside the implementation described here. The report does not promote a code prototype into an empirical literature result.

\subsection{MiniMaintenanceEnv}

A one-item teaching Markov decision process. Operate and replace actions expose the basic observation, transition, reward and episode contract before the fleet model is introduced.

\paragraph{Source lines 23--39.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=17,breakanywhere=true]{python}
class MiniMaintenanceEnv:
    """One aircraft with one replaceable item and two high-level actions.
    Actions:
        0 = operate for one day
        1 = ground for one day and replace the item
    Health is an integer in {0, 1, 2, 3}; 3 is new and 0 is failed.
    A successful operation earns +5. If operation ends at health 0, it earns
    -12 instead. Grounding/replacement earns -4 and restores health to 3.
    Operating wear is 1, plus one extra unit with probability shock_prob.
    The episode ends after ``horizon`` days. Failure itself does not end it:
    the policy can ground and restore the item on a later day.
    """
    OPERATE = 0
    GROUND_AND_REPLACE = 1
\end{minted}

    def reset(self, *, seed: int | None=None, initial_health: int=3):
        """Start an episode and return (observation, info).
        A seed makes subsequent stochastic wear reproducible. Calling reset
        without a seed keeps the current generator stream.
        """
        if initial_health not in (0, 1, 2, 3):
            raise ValueError('initial_health must be 0, 1, 2, or 3')
        if seed is not None:
            self._rng.seed(seed)
        self.health = initial_health
        self.day = 0
        self._needs_reset = False
        return (self._observation(), {'day': self.day})
\end{minted}

    def step(self, action: int):
        """Return (next_observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info)."""
        if self._needs_reset:
            raise RuntimeError('call reset() before step(), including after an episode')
        if action not in (self.OPERATE, self.GROUND_AND_REPLACE):
            raise ValueError('action must be 0 (operate) or 1 (ground/replace)')
        previous_health = self.health
        if action == self.OPERATE:
            extra_wear = int(self._rng.random() < self.shock_prob)
            self.health = max(0, self.health - 1 - extra_wear)
            failed = self.health == 0
            reward = -12.0 if failed else 5.0
            info = {'event': 'failed_operation' if failed else 'successful_operation', 'wear': previous_health - self.health, 'failed': failed, 'grounded': False}
        else:
            self.health = 3
            reward = -4.0
            info = {'event': 'grounded_and_replaced', 'wear': 0, 'failed': False, 'grounded': True}
        self.day += 1
\end{minted}

\subsection{rollout}

Run a tiny-environment episode, retaining transitions so state, action, reward and termination can be inspected.

\paragraph{Source lines 108--119.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=90,breakanywhere=true]{python}
def rollout(env: MiniMaintenanceEnv, policy, *, seed: int=0):
    """Execute one episode; policy receives observation and returns an action."""
    observation, _info = env.reset(seed=seed)
    rows: list[dict] = []
    while True:
        action = policy(observation)
        next_observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
        rows.append({'observation': observation, 'action': action, 'reward': reward, 'next_observation': next_observation, 'event': info['event'], 'terminated': terminated, 'truncated': truncated})
        observation = next_observation
        if terminated or truncated:
            break
    return rows
\end{minted}

\subsection{valid\_action}

Check the conditional tuple contract before a small-example transition can execute.

\paragraph{Source lines 130--146.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=107,breakanywhere=true]{python}
def valid_action(action: tuple[int, int, int]) -> bool:
    """Action is (ground, engine_mask, component_mask).
    Engine bits 0 and 1 represent engines 0 and 1. Component bits 0-1
    represent engine 0; bits 2-3 represent engine 1. A selected engine must
    contain at least one selected component, and no unselected engine may
    receive component work.
    """
    if len(action) != 3 or any((type(x) is not int for x in action)):
        return False
    ground, engines, components = action
    if ground == 0:
        return engines == 0 and components == 0
    if ground != 1 or not 1 <= engines <= 3 or (not 1 <= components <= 15):
        return False
    selected_engines = sum((1 << engine for engine in range(2) if components & 3 << 2 * engine))
    return engines == selected_engines
\end{minted}

\subsection{ConditionalMaintenanceEnv.step}

\paragraph{Source lines 174--191.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=144,breakanywhere=true]{python}
    def step(self, action):
        if self._needs_reset:
            raise RuntimeError('reset before stepping')
        if not valid_action(action):
            raise ValueError(f'infeasible hierarchical action: {action}')
        ground, engines, components = action
        if ground:
            for index in range(4):
                if components & 1 << index:
                    self.health[index] = 3
            n_engines = engines.bit_count()
            n_components = components.bit_count()
            reward = -3.0 - 2.0 * n_engines - 1.0 * n_components
            event = 'grounded_and_replaced'
        else:
            self.health = [max(0, h - 1) for h in self.health]
            reward = -15.0 if 0 in self.health else 8.0
            event = 'failed_operation' if reward < 0 else 'successful_operation'
\end{minted}

\subsection{FleetMaintenanceEnv}

The physical fleet simulator. It owns true health, synthetic sensors, particle beliefs, inventory, heterogeneous resources, jobs, stable aircraft identities, event metrics and the daily clock. Policy networks read observations and cannot replace committed job definitions.

\paragraph{Source lines 324--339.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=272,breakanywhere=true]{python}
class FleetMaintenanceEnv(gym.Env):
    """Action row: ground, engines, bundle0, bundle1, crew_mask, shop, order, priority.
    Engine mask bits 0/1 select engines. Each bundle has six component bits.
    Crew bit i selects member CR-(i+1); workshop remains a single resource index.
    Crew work rates add; workshop factors multiply component work, not setup.
    Resource factors are synthetic teaching assumptions, not calibrated estimates.
    aircraft_plates[i] identifies aircraft i in every state array and action row.
    Plates are synthetic fleet-local identifiers, independent of operating status.
    Reset starts a new simulated history while retaining the index-to-plate mapping.
    Resources are assigned to complete plans, in selected priority order.
    Unfunded/conflicting proposals are rejected and logged; no partial repairs.
    A busy aircraft's row is ignored: the committed plan cannot be overwritten.
    Mandatory grounding uses observed lower health quantiles, not hidden health.
    """
    metadata = {'render_modes': ['ansi']}
\end{minted}

    def __init__(self, config: Config | None=None, render_mode=None):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config or Config()
        self.render_mode = render_mode
        n = self.config.aircraft
        self.aircraft_plates = tuple(f'AC-{i + 1:03d}' for i in range(n))
        self.crew_ids = tuple(f'CR-{i + 1:03d}' for i in range(self.config.crews))
        self.workshop_ids = tuple(f'WS-{i + 1:03d}' for i in range(self.config.workshops))
        self.crew_time_factors = tuple(self.config.crew_time_factors) or tuple((0.8, 1.0, 1.25)[i % 3] for i in range(self.config.crews))
        self.workshop_time_factors = tuple(self.config.workshop_time_factors) or tuple((0.8, 1.0, 1.2)[i % 3] for i in range(self.config.workshops))
        self.row_dims = np.array([2, 4, 64, 64, 1 << self.config.crews, self.config.workshops, 12, n])
        self.action_space = spaces.MultiDiscrete(np.tile(self.row_dims, (n, 1)))
        self.local_size = 70
        self.public_size = 10 + 2 * self.config.crews + 2 * self.config.workshops
        self.observation_space = spaces.Box(0.0, 1.0, shape=(n * self.local_size + self.public_size,), dtype=np.float32)
        self._done = True

\subsection{FleetMaintenanceEnv.reset}

Start an episode, initialize random streams/state, and return the initial observation and diagnostic information.

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=303,breakanywhere=true]{python}
    def reset(self, *, seed=None, options=None):
        super().reset(seed=seed)
        cfg = self.config
        # Physical events, belief updates, and exposure tapes use separate random streams.
        seeds = np.random.SeedSequence(seed).spawn(3)
        self.physical_rng = np.random.default_rng(seeds[0])
        self.filter_rng = np.random.default_rng(seeds[1])
        tape_rng = np.random.default_rng(seeds[2])
        self.day = 0
        self.health = np.clip(cfg.initial_health + self.physical_rng.normal(0, 0.025, (cfg.aircraft, 2, 6)), 0.1, 1)
        if options and 'health' in options:
            health = np.asarray(options['health'], dtype=float)
            if health.shape != self.health.shape or not np.isfinite(health).all() or np.any((health < 0) | (health > 1)):
                raise ValueError('initial health must have shape (aircraft,2,6), in [0,1]')
            self.health = health.copy()
        self.exposure = tape_rng.uniform(0.75, 1.35, cfg.aircraft)
        self.measurements = self._sensor_model(self.health, self.exposure[:, None, None])
        self.measurements += self.physical_rng.normal(0, 1, self.measurements.shape) * self.sensor_noise
\end{minted}

    @staticmethod
    def _sensor_model(health, exposure):
        """Toy performance mapping; health decreases efficiency and raises heat."""
        efficiency = EFFICIENCY_BASE + EFFICIENCY_GAIN * health
        temperature = TEMPERATURE_BASE_C + TEMPERATURE_HEALTH_GAIN_C * (1 - health) + TEMPERATURE_EXPOSURE_GAIN_C * (exposure - 1)
        return np.stack([efficiency, temperature], axis=-1)
\end{minted}

    @staticmethod
    def _invert_sensor_metrics(measurements, exposure):
        """Initialization only: fuse two noisy inverse mappings with equal weight."""
        from_efficiency = (measurements[..., 0] - EFFICIENCY_BASE) / EFFICIENCY_GAIN
        from_temperature = 1 - (measurements[..., 1] - TEMPERATURE_BASE_C - TEMPERATURE_EXPOSURE_GAIN_C * (exposure - 1)) / TEMPERATURE_HEALTH_GAIN_C
        return np.clip(0.5 * (from_efficiency + from_temperature), 0, 1)

\subsection{FleetMaintenanceEnv.\_observation}

Encode this environment's current policy-visible state. In the fleet model this includes belief summaries, committed plans, sensor age and public resources, rather than true health.

\paragraph{Source lines 440--454.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=374,breakanywhere=true]{python}
    def _observation(self):
        mean = self.particles.mean(-1)
        std = self.particles.std(-1)
        low = np.quantile(self.particles, 0.1, axis=-1)
        rows = []
        for a in range(self.config.aircraft):
            j = self.jobs.get(a)
            committed = [j.plan.engine_mask / 3, j.plan.bundles[0] / 63, j.plan.bundles[1] / 63, j.plan.crew_mask / ((1 << self.config.crews) - 1), j.plan.workshop / max(1, self.config.workshops - 1), j.plan.order_start / 11] if j else [0.0] * 6
            rows.append(np.concatenate([mean[a].ravel(), std[a].ravel(), low[a].ravel(), [self.exposure[a] / 1.5, float(j is not None), min(1, j.remaining / 60) if j else 0], committed, self.measurements[a, :, :, 0].ravel(), ((self.measurements[a, :, :, 1] - TEMPERATURE_MIN_C) / (TEMPERATURE_MAX_C - TEMPERATURE_MIN_C)).ravel(), [(self.day - self.last_flight_day[a]) / self.config.horizon]]))
        free, shops = self.resource_state()
        public = [self.day / self.config.horizon, free / self.config.crews, len(shops) / self.config.workshops, (self.config.replenish_days - self.day % self.config.replenish_days) / self.config.replenish_days, *np.clip(self.stock / self.config.aircraft, 0, 1)]
        crew_mask = self.available_crew_mask()
        public.extend([float(bool(crew_mask & (1 << i))) for i in range(self.config.crews)] + [1 / (1 + factor) for factor in self.crew_time_factors])
        public.extend([float(i in shops) for i in range(self.config.workshops)] + [1 / (1 + factor) for factor in self.workshop_time_factors])
        return np.asarray(np.concatenate([np.asarray(rows).ravel(), public]), dtype=np.float32)
\end{minted}

    def validate_row(self, aircraft, row):
        ground, engines, b0, b1, crew_mask, shop, order, priority = map(int, row)
        if not ground:
            return None if engines == b0 == b1 == 0 else 'work_without_grounding'
        actual = int(b0 != 0) + 2 * int(b1 != 0)
        if not actual or engines != actual:

\subsection{FleetMaintenanceEnv.\_start\_job}

Check proposed work against aircraft/resource/stock availability; accept and reserve a committed job or record rejection. Store resource-derived task completion timing at acceptance.

\paragraph{Source lines 467--484.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=399,breakanywhere=true]{python}
    def _start_job(self, aircraft, row):
        _, engines, b0, b1, crew_mask, shop, order, priority = map(int, row)
        plan = Plan(aircraft, engines, (b0, b1), crew_mask, shop, order, priority)
        tasks = [(e, c) for e, b in enumerate((b0, b1)) for c in range(6) if b & 1 << c]
        tasks.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0] * 6 + x[1] - order) % 12)
        needed = np.bincount([c for _, c in tasks], minlength=6)
        _, shops = self.resource_state()
        if crew_mask & self.available_crew_mask() != crew_mask or shop not in shops:
            return ('resource_conflict', 0.0)
        if np.any(needed > self.stock):
            return ('spare_shortage', 0.0)
        work_rate = sum(1 / factor for i, factor in enumerate(self.crew_time_factors) if crew_mask & (1 << i))
        duration = self.config.setup_days
        completion_days = []
        for _, component in tasks:
            duration += max(1, math.ceil(LABOR_DAYS[component] * self.workshop_time_factors[shop] / work_rate))
            completion_days.append(duration)
        self.stock -= needed
\end{minted}

\subsection{FleetMaintenanceEnv.\_update\_filter}

Predict component-health particles under the assumed wear/shock prior, score the synthetic measurements and resample. This is approximate independent marginal filtering, not an RUL forecast.

\paragraph{Source lines 490--508.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=421,breakanywhere=true]{python}
    def _update_filter(self, aircraft, measurements):
        """Bootstrap particle filter with noisy observations and shock-mixture prior.
        The estimator does not receive true event type, severity or hidden health.
        It is a deliberately simple independent-component filter, not Emanuele's.
        """
        cfg = self.config
        p = self.particles[aircraft]
        wear = WEAR[None, :, None] * self.exposure[aircraft] * cfg.wear_scale
        p -= wear * self.filter_rng.normal(1, 0.12, p.shape)
        bird = self.filter_rng.random((2, 1, cfg.particles)) < cfg.bird_probability
        hail = self.filter_rng.random((2, 1, cfg.particles)) < cfg.hail_probability
        bseverity = self.filter_rng.uniform(0.1, 0.35, (2, 1, cfg.particles))
        hseverity = self.filter_rng.uniform(0.1, 0.35, (2, 1, cfg.particles))
        p -= bird * bseverity * np.array([1, 0.5, 0.15, 0, 0, 0])[None, :, None]
        p -= hail * hseverity * np.array([0.7, 0.4, 0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1])[None, :, None]
        p -= (self.filter_rng.random((1, 1, cfg.particles)) < cfg.weather_probability) * wear * 2
        np.clip(p, 0, 1, out=p)
        predicted_efficiency = EFFICIENCY_BASE + EFFICIENCY_GAIN * p
\end{minted}

    def step(self, action):
        if self._done:
            raise RuntimeError('reset before step, including after episode completion')
        a = np.asarray(action)
        if not np.issubdtype(a.dtype, np.integer) or not self.action_space.contains(a):
            raise ValueError('action outside MultiDiscrete space')
        cfg = self.config
        low = np.quantile(self.particles, 0.1, axis=-1)
        mandatory = low.min(axis=(1, 2)) <= cfg.mandatory_health
        costs = 0.0
        events = []
        rejected = []
        completed = []
        grounded = set(self.jobs)
        for aircraft in sorted(range(cfg.aircraft), key=lambda i: (-int(a[i, 7]), i)):
            if aircraft in self.jobs:
                continue
            reason = self.validate_row(aircraft, a[aircraft])
\end{minted}

\subsection{threshold\_action}

A fixed threshold controller for the original full-action interface. It selects observed-condition-driven repairs and feasible resources; it contains no trained neural parameters.

\paragraph{Source lines 605--622.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=532,breakanywhere=true]{python}
def threshold_action(env, observation, threshold=0.65, bundle_threshold=0.75):
    """Feasible rule using only observations, not hidden health or event diagnostics."""
    rows, public = env.split_observation(observation)
    action = env.idle_action()
    free_mask = sum(1 << i for i in range(env.config.crews) if public[10 + i] > 0.5)
    shop_offset = 10 + 2 * env.config.crews
    shops = sorted((i for i in range(env.config.workshops) if public[shop_offset + i] > 0.5), key=lambda i: env.workshop_time_factors[i])
    stock = np.rint(public[4:10] * env.config.aircraft).astype(int)
    scores = rows[:, 24:36].min(1)
    rank = np.argsort(scores)
    for priority, aircraft in enumerate(rank[::-1]):
        action[aircraft, 7] = priority
    for aircraft in rank:
        if rows[aircraft, 37] > 0.5 or scores[aircraft] > threshold or not free_mask or (not shops):
            continue
        health = rows[aircraft, :12].reshape(2, 6)
        selected = health <= bundle_threshold
        if not selected.any():
\end{minted}

\subsection{\_fleet\_observation\_tensor}

Convert to float32, batch a single observation and enforce the declared global width without allocating per-aircraft actor context.

\paragraph{Source lines 668--675.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=583,breakanywhere=true]{python}
def _fleet_observation_tensor(observation, width, error_message):
    """Validate global inputs without allocating per-aircraft actor features."""
    obs = torch.as_tensor(observation, dtype=torch.float32)
    if obs.ndim == 1:
        obs = obs.unsqueeze(0)
    if obs.ndim != 2 or obs.shape[1] != width:
        raise ValueError(error_message)
    return obs
\end{minted}

\subsection{FleetActorCritic}

The full-action policy family. One actor is reused across aircraft; optional global encoding and previous-field conditioning distinguish flat, conditional and shared modes. A scalar global critic and a fleet-joint likelihood support the original PPO trainer.

\paragraph{Source lines 678--688.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=591,breakanywhere=true]{python}
class FleetActorCritic(nn.Module):
    """Central critic + flat, conditional, or parameter-shared aircraft actors.
    shared: local aircraft estimates + public resource counts. Parameters reused
    across aircraft; a central deterministic resolver enforces resource capacity.
    conditional: global actor context and masked dependent action distributions.
    flat: shared global features with no learned conditioning on preceding choices.
    All methods use the same logical masks; scarce-resource conflicts are resolved
    by the simulator and reported separately from structural feasibility.
    All act daily and obey pre-start commitment; this is not temporal HRL.
    """
\end{minted}

    def __init__(self, env: FleetMaintenanceEnv, mode='conditional', goal_size=0):
        super().__init__()
        if mode not in ('flat', 'conditional', 'shared'):
            raise ValueError(mode)
        self.mode = mode
        self.n = env.config.aircraft
        self.local = env.local_size
        self.public = env.public_size
        self.dims = env.row_dims.tolist()
        self.mandatory = env.config.mandatory_health
        self.goal_size = goal_size
        size = env.observation_space.shape[0]
        # Keep legacy registered layers/state keys even when this mode does not execute them.
        self.global_encoder = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(size, 64), nn.Tanh())
        in_size = self.local + self.public + (0 if mode == 'shared' else 64) + goal_size

    def act(self, obs, actions=None, deterministic=False, goal=None):
        if obs.ndim == 1:
            obs = obs.unsqueeze(0)
        batch = obs.shape[0]
        local = obs[:, :-self.public].reshape(batch, self.n, self.local)
        public = obs[:, -self.public:].unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, self.n, -1)
        features = [local, public]
        if self.goal_size:
            if goal is None:
                raise ValueError('goal-conditioned worker requires a goal')
            features.append(goal.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, self.n, -1))
        if self.mode != 'shared':
            features.append(self.global_encoder(obs).unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, self.n, -1))
        h = self.actor(torch.cat(features, -1))
        previous = None if self.mode == 'flat' else torch.zeros(batch, self.n, 8, device=obs.device)
        logprob = torch.zeros(batch, device=obs.device)
        entropy = torch.zeros_like(logprob)
        result = []
\end{minted}

class LearnedOptionActorCritic(nn.Module):

    option collapse/credit assignment require later ablations and diagnostics.
    """

    def act(self, obs, actions=None, deterministic=False):
        if obs.ndim == 1:
            obs = obs.unsqueeze(0)
        macro = None if actions is None else actions[:, 0]
        plan = None if actions is None else actions[:, 1:].reshape(-1, self.n, 8)
        option, lp, entropy, value = self.manager.act(obs, macro, deterministic)
        goal = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(option, num_classes=4).float()
        plan, worker_lp, worker_entropy, _ = self.worker.act(obs, plan, deterministic, goal)
        composite = torch.cat([option.unsqueeze(-1), plan.flatten(1)], -1)
        return (composite, lp + worker_lp, entropy + worker_entropy, value)

\subsection{mappo\_agent\_inputs}

Construct exactly the actor information views used by the two MAPPO assignments. Aircraft views contain one local row plus public state; component views collect their component-specific features across the fleet.

\paragraph{Source lines 822--839.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=720,breakanywhere=true]{python}
def mappo_agent_inputs(observation, aircraft, local_size, public_size, assignment):
    """Build restricted actor inputs from observed beliefs, never hidden health."""
    obs = _fleet_observation_tensor(observation, aircraft * local_size + public_size,
                                    'incorrect fleet observation shape')
    local = obs[:, :aircraft * local_size].reshape(-1, aircraft, local_size)
    public = obs[:, -public_size:]
    if assignment == 'aircraft':
        # Each aircraft sees only its own row plus the common resource board.
        return torch.cat([local, public.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, aircraft, -1)], dim=-1)
    if assignment != 'component':
        raise ValueError('assignment must be aircraft or component')
    # Ten own-component values: two engines x mean/std/lower/efficiency/temperature.
    indices = [[c, c + 6, c + 12, c + 18, c + 24, c + 30,
                c + 45, c + 51, c + 57, c + 63, 36, 37, 38, 69] for c in range(6)]
    own = torch.stack([local[:, :, ix] for ix in indices], dim=1)
    # A broadcast safety-criticality report is an explicit cross-component message.
    criticality = local[:, :, 24:36].amin(-1)
    board = criticality[:, None, :, None].expand(-1, 6, -1, -1)
\end{minted}

\subsection{MultiAgentFleetEnv}

A request adapter with aircraft or component-type ownership. It converts agent proposals into full fleet actions through a deterministic stock/resource broker. Shared team reward does not remove the broker or create learned communication.

\paragraph{Source lines 844--854.}

\begin{minted}[firstnumber=740,breakanywhere=true]{python}
class MultiAgentFleetEnv:
    """Cooperative dictionary API around the same physical fleet simulator.
    Aircraft agents propose two six-bit bundles; six component agents each
    propose a two-engine mask for every aircraft. Both cover the same twelve
    replacement bits per aircraft. They do not learn crew/shop/order choices.
    A public request board and deterministic centralized dispatcher coordinate
    execution. This is decentralized proposal generation with centralized
    arbitration, not fully decentralized resource allocation or learned messaging.
    This small adapter is not a PettingZoo/RLlib API implementation.
    """
\end{minted}

    def __init__(self, config=None, assignment='aircraft'):
        if assignment not in ('aircraft', 'component'):
            raise ValueError('assignment must be aircraft or component')
        self.env = FleetMaintenanceEnv(config)
        self.assignment = assignment
        self.agent_ids = self.env.aircraft_plates if assignment == 'aircraft' else COMPONENTS
        self.num_agents = len(self.agent_ids)
        dims = [64, 64] if assignment == 'aircraft' else [4] * self.env.config.aircraft
        self.action_spaces = {agent: spaces.MultiDiscrete(dims) for agent in self.agent_ids}

        self.observation_spaces = {agent: spaces.Box(0, 1, shape=(width,), dtype=np.float32) for agent in self.agent_ids}
        self.central_observation = None
        self.coordination_deferrals = 0

    def compose_action(self, actions):
        """Merge owned requests and allocate resources using observed data only."""
        if self.central_observation is None:
            raise RuntimeError('reset before composing agent proposals')
        if not isinstance(actions, dict) or set(actions) != set(self.agent_ids):
